intermediate_answers.answer: The capital city of Australia is Canberra. It was selected as the site for the new capital in 1909 following the federation of the Australian colonies in 1901. The city was designed by American architects Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin, and the federal Parliament officially transferred from Melbourne to Canberra on May 9, 1927.

The selection of Canberra as the capital was a strategic compromise between Australia's two largest cities, Sydney and Melbourne, both of which vied for the title after the Commonwealth of Australia was established on January 1, 1901 [What is the capital of Australia? *   **Constitutional Requirements:** The Australian Constitution mandated that the capital be located at least 100 miles (160 km) from Sydney, with the federal Parliament sitting in Melbourne until the new capital was completed [Sydney isn't the capital of Australia! - Ovolo Hotels — ovolohotels.com](https://ovolohotels.com/ovolo/blog/sydney-isnt-the-capital-of-australia).

    *   **1913:** Construction began, and the city was officially named by Lady Denman on March 12, 1913 [Canberra | History, Map, Population, Climate, & Facts - Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/place/Canberra) [Canberra, the Seat of Government | National Capital Authority — www.nca.gov.au](https://www.nca.gov.au/education/canberras-history/canberra-seat-government).
    *   **1927:** The federal Parliament officially transferred from Melbourne to Canberra [Canberra | History, Map, Population, Climate, & Facts - Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/place/Canberra).
</details>

## Geography and Administrative Status
Canberra is located in the Australian Capital Territory (ACT) in southeastern Australia, approximately 150 miles (240 km) southwest of Sydney [Canberra | History, Map, Population, Climate, & Facts - Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/place/Canberra). The city is situated on the Molonglo River and is home to major national institutions [Canberra | History, Map, Population, Climate, & Facts - Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/place/Canberra).

<details>
<summary>Key facts about Canberra's status and features</summary>

*   **Etymology:** The name "Canberra" is derived from an Aboriginal term meaning "meeting place" [Canberra | History, Map, Population, Climate, & Facts - Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/place/Canberra).
*   **Key Institutions:** The city houses the Parliament House (opened in 1988), the High Court of Australia, the National Library of Australia, and the Australian National War Memorial [Canberra | History, Map, Population, Climate, & Facts - Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/place/Canberra).
*   **Urban Planning:** The city was designed with specific functional zones for administration, business, and trade, and features an ornamental water axis known as Lake Burley Griffin, created in 1963 [Canberra | History, Map, Population, Climate, & Facts - Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/place/Canberra) [What is the capital of Australia? If you thought it was Sydney, keep ... — youtooproject.com](https://youtooproject.com/en/blog/australia-en/capital-of-australia-canberra).
</details>

## Key Takeaways
*   **Official Capital:** Canberra is the federal capital of Australia.
*   **Common Misconception:** Sydney and Melbourne are frequently mistaken for the capital due to their size and prominence, but neither holds the title.
*   **Strategic Origins:** Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne, fulfilling a constitutional requirement to be located away from Sydney.
*   **Development:** The city was designed by Walter Burley Griffin and Marion Mahony Griffin, with the federal government moving there in 1927.
